title: Perfect global tests of an infinitesimal quasi-coherent module limit
statement:
Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Separated, finite type and proper morphisms use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has a presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Base-flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the corresponding local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means there exist a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ such that $i_*G\simeq F$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent, meaning every element of each kernel is nilpotent, and set $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and finitely presented, put $X_n=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. For every $n\geq1$ let $M_n$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module, flat over $A_n$, with support proper over $A_n$, with specified isomorphisms $M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology. Regard $M_n$ as a module on $X$ by direct image along $X_n\hookrightarrow X$; the given transition isomorphisms followed by quotient maps define its inverse-system maps. The symbol $R\varprojlim_{D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}}M_n$ denotes the homotopy inverse limit in this full derived subcategory: it fits into the product triangle $K\to\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\to K[1]$, with products taken in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ and projections $q_n:K\to M_n$ induced by the first arrow. Here the shift has $n$th component equal to the transition map composed with the $(n+1)$st projection. Let $K$ be this homotopy inverse limit [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-derived-limit]. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be perfect: etale locally it is represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. The complex $C_E=R\Gamma(X,K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}E)$ is perfect over $A$, meaning represented by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Write $i_n:X_n\hookrightarrow X$ and $E_n=Li_n^*E$. There is a canonical isomorphism in $D(A_n)$
$$\beta_{E,n}:C_E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X_n,M_n\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X_n}}^{\mathbf L}E_n).$$
It is the scalar-extension adjunct of $R\Gamma(q_n\otimes1_E)$ followed by the projection-formula identification
$$R\Gamma(X,i_{n,*}M_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}E)\simeq R\Gamma(X_n,M_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}E_n).$$
Equivalently, after this identification, the scalar-extension adjunct to $R\Gamma(q_n\otimes1_E)$ is itself an isomorphism to the left-hand expression $R\Gamma(X,i_{n,*}M_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}E)$, with its $A_n$-action. The maps are natural in all morphisms of perfect $E$, and after scalar extension $A_n\to A_{n-1}$ their transition squares commute with the specified isomorphisms of the modules. Tensor pullback is derived using K-flat resolutions; global sections are derived using K-injective resolutions.

proof.text: Put $f_n:X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ and $T_n=R\Gamma(X_n,M_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}E_n)$. Base change preserves finite presentation, so $f_n$ is finitely presented; derived pullback preserves perfect objects, so $E_n$ is perfect. The proper carrier in the hypothesis contains the closed support of $M_n$: its defining ideal kills $M_n$, hence the annihilator support is contained in that carrier. The proper-support closed-operations lemma makes this annihilator support proper too. Thus the bounded complex $M_n[0]$ has exactly the finite-presentation, relative flatness and proper-support hypotheses of the tensor-perfect direct-image theorem.

source.place: Tag 0CX6 (lemma-compute-against-perfect), proof, tensor form of the global Hom argument.

proof.text: Apply the proper-support tensor-perfect theorem to $(f_n,E_n,M_n[0])$. Its derived direct image is perfect on $\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. By derived direct-image composition its derived global sections over $\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ are $T_n$, and the affine etale derived-module equivalence identifies it with the realization of $T_n$; the etale/Zariski derived equivalence, etale detection of perfectness and the affine bounded-projective criterion show that $T_n$ is a perfect $A_n$-complex. Apply flat-complex base change to $f_n$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A_{n-1}\to\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. Its coefficient pullback is ordinary tensor pullback of $M_n$, identified with $M_{n-1}$ by the specified isomorphism, while $E_n$ pulls back to $E_{n-1}$. The affine pullback/tensor comparison, transported through the etale/Zariski equivalence, therefore gives an isomorphism $\gamma_{n-1}:T_n\otimes_{A_n}^{\mathbf L}A_{n-1}\to T_{n-1}$. Use as transition its scalar-restriction adjunct, so the tower maps are the ones induced by the quotient maps and the specified module isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0CX6 (lemma-compute-against-perfect), proof, tensor form of the global Hom argument.

proof.text: Apply the nil-kernel ring-tower reconstruction lemma to $(A_n,T_n,\gamma_{n-1})$. Every $T_n$ is perfect, all ring maps are surjective with locally nilpotent kernels, and $A=\varprojlim A_n$ by hypothesis. Thus $T=R\varprojlim T_n$ is perfect over $A$, and its projection adjuncts $\rho_n:T\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n\to T_n$ are isomorphisms. This uses the all-stages-perfect case, without asserting that the rings are powers of a single ideal.

source.place: Tag 0CX6 (lemma-compute-against-perfect), proof, tensor form of the global Hom argument.

proof.text:
Set $H_n=i_{n,*}M_n$. On a scheme chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$, $i_n$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A A_n)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, a quotient-ring closed immersion, so it is affine and quasi-compact separated by the closed-immersion chart definition. Its direct image is quasi-coherent, and affine module higher-image vanishing gives $Ri_{n,*}M_n=H_n[0]$. The quasi-coherent derived projection formula for $i_n$, followed by derived direct-image composition, gives the canonical isomorphism
$$\pi_{E,n}:F_E(H_n)=R\Gamma(X,H_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}E)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_n.$$
The projection formula is the counit-induced comparison; hence its naturality in the coefficient module and derived composition identify $F_E(H_n\to H_{n-1})$ with the transition of step 2 under these isomorphisms. No flatness of $i_n$ or $X/A$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0CX6 (lemma-compute-against-perfect), proof, tensor form of the global Hom argument.

proof.text:
Use the product triangle and projections of the derived-limit node for $K$. The perfect tensor global-sections lemma applies since $X/A$ is quasi-compact quasi-separated. Applying it to this triangle and then the identifications $\pi_{E,n}$ gives an isomorphism $\theta_E:C_E\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ with $p_n\theta_E=\pi_{E,n}R\Gamma(q_n\otimes1_E)$. Consequently $C_E$ is perfect and
$$\rho_n\circ(\theta_E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n):C_E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}T_n$$
is an isomorphism. By scalar-extension adjunction and the displayed projection equality, this composite is exactly $\beta_{E,n}$ specified in the statement. Composing with $\pi_{E,n}^{-1}$ gives precisely its equivalent formulation on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0CX6 (lemma-compute-against-perfect), proof, tensor form of the global Hom argument.

proof.text: For a morphism $v:E\to E'$, the identity $(q_n\otimes1_{E'})(1_K\otimes v)=(1_{H_n}\otimes v)(q_n\otimes1_E)$, naturality of the projection formula and scalar-extension adjunction give the naturality square for $\beta_{E,n}$. For successive levels, both $\beta_{E,n-1}$ and $\gamma_{n-1}\circ(\beta_{E,n}\otimes_{A_n}^{\mathbf L}A_{n-1})$ have, after scalar restriction and the canonical associativity identifications, adjunct $\pi_{E,n-1}R\Gamma(q_{n-1}\otimes1_E)$: substitute $q_{n-1}=t_nq_n$ and the transition identification of step 4. The adjunction bijection makes the two maps equal. This proves the specified transition square, including its module isomorphism, and proves all asserted compatibilities.
